title: Week of Sep 28 - Oct 4
subtitle: Block 4, build week 1 of 3. Variation B, endurance-led: running builds 22, 25, 27 while the lifts rotate to pause squat, deficit deadlift and seated dumbbell press, with flat bench staying for the 225 track. This is a calibration week for the new lifts, each one ramps to a single top set at about 2 in reserve. 22 miles with the first threshold session since the time trial and the Saturday long run debut at 6.
goals: Block 4 in one line: only one quality gets pushed per block, and this block it is the running. Mileage builds 22, 25, 27 with a deload around 19. The lifts are variations of the same patterns at submaximal loads, which is exactly what a variation block is for. Bench stays flat bench because of the 225 track.

Calibration, lift by lift. Each new lift ramps to ONE top set at about 2 in reserve, and whatever you actually hit becomes next week's starting number. Pause squat is the barbell back squat with a 2s dead stop in the hole: no bounce, so you have to hold position, which is the direct fix for the knees caving that you noticed at 225. It runs roughly 15% lighter than a normal back squat for the same reps, so 175x5 is a real set, and you haven't squatted since Sep 14. Deficit deadlift is off a 1.5 to 2 inch plate and runs about 85 to 90% of conventional, so 255x4 after the 275 triples last Friday. Seated DB press replaces strict OHP and should land somewhere around 45s x8.

Bench, road to 225: Wednesday is the 205x2 that got pushed a week. Short ramp (155x3, 175x2, 195x1), then 205x2 at 2 or fewer in reserve, then 2x4 at 180. If 205 moves with 2 or more in reserve, the attempt can come up a week to Oct 7; otherwise Oct 5 week is 215x1 and the attempt stays Oct 14. Friday is paused bench 3x5 at 165. Last week's 185 triples and 155 paused fours say you're right where you left off. Safety arms at chest height every heavy set.

Running, 22 miles: Mon 1.5, Tue 5 (threshold), Wed 1.5, Thu 4, Fri 1.5, Sat 6, Sun 2.5. The only quality touch is Tuesday, 4x5 min at 170 to 178 with 2 min jogs, one notch under the 6 minute reps you ran before the time trial. Strides Sunday are free. Everything else is Zone 2.

Easy HR is still a few beats high, so go by the number this week, not the pace. Thursday's 3.5 at 8:35/mi averaged 160 and Saturday's 4 at 8:40 averaged 154, while Sunday's 2.9 at a truly easy pace was 142. So easy means 150 or under even if that is 9:30 pace. The plasma volume is still refilling after the illness, and the easy-run HR is the readout for when it's done. When 8:40 pace reads 150 again, you're back.

Saturday: the long run debuts at 6 miles, 27% of the week, run first. Then calisthenics condensed behind it: the pull-up max set (the series continues, but it's post-run from here on, so a rep or two under 19 is the expected reading, not a regression), push-ups 25/20/15, dips 3x6, and the inverted row + pike pair. If the weather takes out the outdoor bar again, do the calisthenics at the gym rather than dropping them.

Volume, since you asked: 89 planned sets and about 64,000 lb on the app's volume graph, within about 2% of the Sep 7 build week (87 sets logged, 65,489 lb) and sits at the top of your 75 to 90 build band. What makes it up: squat day ~23k, bench day ~21k, deadlift day ~14k, Saturday ~6k. The top sets are lighter than Sep 7 because they're calibration numbers on new lifts, so the volume comes from a flatter ramp, heavier hip thrusts, and three added pieces: back extensions Monday, lat pulldowns Wednesday, a fourth paused bench set Friday. Sessions run 55 to 65 minutes. Log the seated DB press as the pair total or the graph will read about 1,300 lb low.

Weight and food: deficit stays at 400, your call, steady out first and change nothing until the post-sickness noise clears. The scale read 185.6 to 187.5 last week against 189 before you got sick. Most of that is water and glycogen from a week of barely eating, and it will probably come back up a pound or two as you eat and train normally. That is not a stall. Log full days. If easy HR is still high next Sunday and the weight is still dropping fast, that's the tripwire and we revisit then.
review: Bridge week. Monday you were still sick and skipped it, the right call. Tuesday 3.01 easy at 149. Wednesday back under the bar: bench 185x3 twice as planned, OHP went to 115x5 (plan said 110), rows 135x8, pull-ups 2x8, 'First weight training since I didn't feel healthy enough on Monday.' Thursday 3.5 at 160, a little quick for where the HR is right now. Friday deadlift ramped to 275x3 twice (plan said 255) and paused bench 155x4, 'Still not feeling particularly great.' Saturday 4 miles at 154, calisthenics washed out by the weather. Sunday evening 2.9 easy at 142. About 16 of 17 miles and 39 of 69 planned sets, with the easy HR coming down across the week. You called it a solid week and the log agrees.
